title: Your containment GameDay
scenario: Design a repeatable fault on one lamp dependency. Show its impact on the catalog or healthy products, then test whether your mitigation contains it.
why: An enabled fallback is not proof of resilience. Show useful results before and after mitigation, including remaining uncertainty.
reproduce: Choose lamp Inventory or Shipping, a delay or disconnect, and a catalog view. A +1500 ms delay can pressure workers; a disconnect can fail aggregation.
ready: {{ready}} Fault only the exposed lamp paths; use chair and desk as healthy comparisons.
assignment: Can you contain a wider failure to the affected product’s missing data?

tasks.title: Define a propagation hypothesis
tasks.instruction: Specify catalog view, dependency, fault/magnitude, healthy comparisons and abort condition. Predict the spread and choose signals that could disprove it.

tasks.title: Record a healthy comparison window
tasks.instruction: Measure all products, catalog time/status, queue and new rejections over a fixed window. Keep traffic unchanged.

tasks.title: Reproduce impact beyond the lamp
tasks.instruction: Apply your fault and repeat the measurements. Identify queuing, rejection or catalog failure. If no wider impact appears, record it and revise your experiment.

tasks.title: Choose a mechanism-specific mitigation
tasks.instruction: Remove the fault. Choose a short timeout for slow calls and fallback/breaker for the affected dependency. Explain the missing-data response; fallback alone does not free workers.

tasks.title: Repeat exactly and recommend
tasks.instruction: Repeat the identical fault and traffic. Compare healthy products, catalog results and missing lamp data. Record probe behavior and rollback. {{cleanup}}

done: A teammate can reproduce the fault, traffic, three-phase measurements, mitigation and rollback.
You demonstrated and measured a wider impact before mitigation, then compared healthy products and catalog usefulness under the identical fault.
You distinguished timeout, breaker and fallback, described remaining uncertainty/probe spikes, and restored all three products.
solution: A valid experiment compares healthy, faulted and mitigated phases under identical fault and traffic, showing wider impact and the remaining trade-off.
Example: add 1500 ms to lamp Shipping during delivery refresh. Retest with a 400 ms timeout plus fallback/breaker.
Chair and desk retain live data; the lamp quote is unavailable. Expect 5-second recovery probes. Compare queue and new rejections.
Distinguish catalog failure from worker pressure. Restore defaults, clear faults and verify live results.

fields.label: Experiment plan
fields.prompt: Name the view, dependency, fault/magnitude, expected impact and abort condition.

fields.label: Fault result
fields.prompt: Record the fault settings and dependency signals. {{measurementGuidance}}

fields.label: {{mitigationLabel}}
fields.prompt: Which settings did you change, and why? {{mitigationGuidance}}

fields.label: Identical-fault validation
fields.prompt: Repeat the same fault and compare results. {{measurementGuidance}}

fields.label: Conclusion, trade-off, and rollback
fields.prompt: What improved? What risk remains? Describe rollback.

overview.title: 4 · Prove useful containment
overview.description: Design an experiment whose mitigation visibly protects the catalog or healthy products, and document its trade-off.
